translations.title: Trilce: Poema XX - To the ras of batiente nata blindada
translations.text:
To the ras of batiente nata blindada
of piedra ideal. For apenas
acerco the 1 to the 1 for not caer.

Ese man mostachoso. Sun,
herrada his única rueda, quinta and perfecta,
and from ella for arriba.
Bulla of botones of bragueta,
                                                libres,
bulla that reprende To vertical subordinada.
The desagüe jurídico. The chirota grata.

But sufro. Allende sufro. Aquende sufro.

And he here is me cae the baba, soy
a bella persona, when
the man guillermosecundario
puja and suda felicidad
to chorros, to the give lustre to the calzado
of his pequeña of tres años.

Engállase the barbado and frota a lado.
The girl in tanto pónese the índice
in the lengua that empieza to deletrear
the enredos of enredos of the enredos,
and unta the other zapato, to escondidas,
with a poquito of saliva and earth,
                                                   but with a poquito
                                                                               not má-
                                                                                  .s.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Yeso
translations.text:
Silence. Here is ha hecho already of night,
        already tras of the cementerio is was the sun;
        here is is llorando to mil pupilas:
        not vuelvas; already murió my heart.
        Silence. Here already all is vestido
        of pain riguroso; and arde apenas,
        as a mal kerosene, esta pasión.


        Primavera vendrá. Cantarás «Eva»
        from a minuto horizontal, from a
        hornillo in that arderán the nardos of Eros.
        ¡Forja there your perdón for the poeta,
        that ha of dolerme still,
        as clavo that cierra a ataúd!


        But… a night of lirismo, your
        buen seno, your mar red
        is azotará with olas of quince años,
        to the see lejos, aviado with recuerdos
        my corsario bajel, my ingratitud.
        Después, your manzanar, your labio dándose,
        and that is aja for mí for the vez última,
        and that muere sangriento of amar mucho,
        as a croquis pagano of Jesús.


        ¡Amada! And cantarás;
        and ha of vibrar the femenino in my soul,
        as in a enlutada catedral.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXXV - Estáis muertos
translations.text:
Estáis muertos.

What extraña manera of estarse muertos. Quienquiera diría not lo
estáis. But, in verdad, estáis muertos, muertos.

Flotáis nadamente detrás of aquesa membrana that, péndula of the
zenit to the nadir, comes and va of crepúsculo to crepúsculo, vibrando ante the
sonora caja of a herida that to vosotros not os duele. Os digo, for, that
the life is in the espejo, and that vosotros sois the original, the death.

Mientras the onda va, mientras the onda comes, cuán impunemente is
is uno dead. Sólo when the aguas is quebrantan in the bordes
enfrentados and is doblan and doblan, entonces os transfiguráis and creyendo
die, percibís the sexta cuerda that already not is vuestra.

Estáis muertos, not habiendo antes vivido jamás. Quienquiera diría
that, not siendo ahora, in other time fuisteis. But, in verdad, vosotros
sois the cadáveres of a life that never was. Sad destino the not haber
sido sino muertos always. The be hoja seca without haber sido green jamás.
Orfandad of orfandades.

And sinembargo, the muertos not son, not pueden be cadáveres of a
life that todavía not han vivido. Ellos murieron always of life.

Estáis muertos.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LVIII - In the celda, in lo sólido, también
translations.text:
In the celda, in lo sólido, también
is acurrucan the rincones.

Arreglo the desnudos that is ajan,
is doblan, is harapan.

Apéome of the caballo jadeante, bufando
líneas of bofetadas and of horizontes;
espumoso pie against tres cascos.
And le ayudo: Anda, animal!

Is tomaría menos, always menos, of lo
that me tocase erogar,
in the celda, in lo líquido.

The compañero of prisión comía the trigo
of the lomas, with my propia cuchara,
when, to the mesa of my padres, child,
me quedaba dormido masticando.

Le soplo to the other:
Return, sal for the other esquina;
apura ...aprisa,... apronta!

E inadvertido aduzco, planeo,
cabe camastro desvencijado, piadoso:
Not creas. Aquel médico was a man sano.

Already not reiré when my mother rece
in infancia and in domingo, to the cuatro
of the madrugada, for the caminantes,
encarcelados,
enfermos
and pobres.

In the redil of niños, already not le asestaré
puñetazos to ninguno of ellos, quien, después,
todavía sangrando, lloraría: The other sábado
you daré of my fiambre, but
not me pegues!
Already not le diré that good.

In the celda, in the gas ilimitado
until redondearse in the condensación,
¿who tropieza for afuera?
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXVIII - He almorzado solo ahora, and not he tenido
translations.text:
He almorzado solo ahora, and not he tenido
mother, ni súplica, ni sírvete, ni water,
ni father that, in the facundo ofertorio
of the choclos, pregunte for his tardanza
of imagen, for the broches mayores of the sonido.

How iba I to almorzar. How me iba to servir
of tales platos distantes esas cosas,
when habráse quebrado the propio hogar,
when not asoma ni mother to the labios.
How iba I to almorzar nonada.

To the mesa of a buen amigo he almorzado
with his father recién llegado of the mundo,
with his canas tías that hablan
in tordillo retinte of porcelana,
bisbiseando for all his viudos alvéolos;
and with cubiertos francos of alegres tiroriros,
because estánse in his casa. Así, ¡what gracia!
And me han dolido the cuchillos
of esta mesa in all the paladar.

The yantar of estas mesas así, in that is prueba
love ajeno in vez of the propio love,
torna earth the brocado that not brinda the
                                                          Mother,
makes golpe the dura deglución; the dulce,
hiel; aceite funéreo, the café.

When already is ha quebrado the propio hogar,
and the sírvete materno not sale of the
tumba,
the cocina to oscuras, the miseria of love.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: And si después of tantas words
translations.text:
¡And si después of tantas words,
        not sobrevive the word!
        ¡Si después of the alas of the pájaros,
        not sobrevive the pájaro parado!
        ¡More valdría, in verdad,
        that is lo coman all and acabemos!


        ¡Haber nacido for live of nuestra death!
        ¡Levantarse of the sky toward the earth
        for his propios desastres
        and espiar the momento of apagar with his shadow his tiniebla!
        ¡More valdría, francamente,
        that is lo coman all and what more gives…!


        ¡And si después of tanta historia, sucumbimos,
        not already of eternidad,
        sino of esas cosas sencillas, as be
        in the casa or ponerse to cavilar!
        ¡And si luego encontramos,
        of buenas to primeras, that vivimos,
        to juzgar for the altura of the astros,
        for the peine and the manchas of the pañuelo!
        ¡More valdría, in verdad,
        that is lo coman all, from luego!


        Is dirá that tenemos
        in uno of the eyes mucha pena
        and también in the other, mucha pena
        and in the dos, when miran, mucha pena…
        Entonces… ¡Claro!… Entonces… ¡ni word!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The dados eternos
translations.text:
For Manuel González Prada, esta
        emoción bravía and selecta, a of the
        that, with more entusiasmo, me ha aplau-
        dido the gran maestro.


        Dios mío, estoy llorando the be that vivo;
        me pesa haber tomádote your pan;
        but este pobre barro pensativo
        not is costra fermentada in your costado:
        ¡tú not tienes Marías that is van!


        Dios mío, si tú hubieras sido man,
        today supieras be Dios;
        but tú, that estuviste always bien,
        not sientes nothing of your creación.
        ¡And the man sí you sufre: the Dios is él!


        Today that in my eyes brujos there is candelas,
        as in a condenado,
        Dios mío, prenderás todas your velas,
        and jugaremos with the old dado.
        Tal vez ¡oh jugador! to the give the suerte
        of the universo all,
        surgirán the ojeras of the Death,
        as dos ases fúnebres of lodo.


        Dios míos, and esta night sorda, obscura,
        already not podrás jugar, because the Earth
        is a dado roído and already redondo
        to fuerza of rodar to the aventura,
        that not puede parar sino in a hueco,
        in the hueco of inmensa sepultura.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXIII - Tahona estuosa of aquellos my bizcochos
translations.text:
Tahona estuosa of aquellos my bizcochos
pura yema infantil innumerable, mother.

Oh your cuatro gorgas, asombrosamente
mal plañidas, mother: your mendigos.
The dos hermanas últimas, Miguel that ha dead
and I arrastrando todavía
a trenza for cada letra of the abecedario.

In the sala of arriba us repartías
of tomorrow, of tarde, of dual estiba,
aquellas ricas hostias of time, for
that ahora us sobrasen
cáscaras of relojes in flexión of the 24
in punto parados.

Mother, and ahora! Ahora, in which alvéolo
quedaría, in what retoño capilar,
cierta migaja that today is me ata to the cuello
and not quiere pass. Today that until
your puros huesos estarán harina
that not habrá in what amasar
¡tierna dulcera of love,
until in the cruda shadow, until in the gran molar
cuya encía late in aquel lácteo hoyuelo
that inadvertido lábrase and pulula ¡tú lo viste tánto!
in the cerradas hands recién nacidas.

Tal the earth oirá in your silenciar,
how us van cobrando all
the alquiler of the mundo where us dejas
and the valor of aquel pan inacabable.
And us lo cobran, when, siendo nosotros
pequeños entonces, as tú verías,
not is lo podíamos haber arrebatado
to nadie; when tú us lo diste,
¿di, mamá?
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LII - And us levantaremos when is us dé
translations.text:
And us levantaremos when is us dé
the gana, aunque mamá all claror
us despierte with cantora
and linda cólera materna.
Nosotros reiremos to hurtadillas of esto,
mordiendo the canto of the tibias colchas
of vicuña ¡and not me vayas to make cosas!

      The humos of the bohíos ¡ah golfillos
in rama! madrugarían to jugar
to the cometas azulinas, azulantes,
and, apañuscando alfarjes and piedras, us darían
his estímulo fragante of boñiga,
                                                 for sacarnos
to the aire nene that not conoce still the letras,
to pelearles the hilos.

Other day querrás pastorear
between your huecos onfalóideos
                              ávidas cavernas,
                        meses nonos,
                              my telones.
Or querrás acompañar to the ancianía
to destapar the toma of a crepúsculo,
for that of day surja
all the water that passes of night.

And llegas muriéndote of risa,
and in the almuerzo musical,
cancha reventada, harina with manteca,
with manteca,
le tomas the pelo to the peón decúbito
that today other vez olvida give the buenos days,
esos his days, buenos with b of baldío,
that insisten in salirle to the pobre
for the culata of the v
dentilabial that the vela in él.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXXV - The encuentro with the amada
translations.text:
The encuentro with the amada
tánto alguna vez, is a simple detalle,
casi a programa hípico in violado,
that of tan largo not is puede doblar bien.

The almuerzo with ella that estaría
poniendo the plato that us gustara yesterday
and is repite ahora,
but with something more of mostaza;
the tenedor absorto, his doneo radiante
of pistilo in mayo, and his verecundia
of to centavito, for quítame allá esa paja.
And the cerveza lírica and nerviosa
to the that celan his dos pezones without lúpulo,
and that not is debe tomar mucho!

And the demás encantos of the mesa
that aquella núbil campaña borda
with his propias baterías germinales
that han operado all the tomorrow,
según me consta, to mí,
amoroso notario of his intimidades,
and with the diez varillas mágicas
of his dedos pancreáticos.

Woman that, without pensar in nothing more allá,
suelta the mirlo and is pone to conversarnos
his words tiernas
as lancinantes lechugas recién cortadas.

Other vaso, and me voy. And us marchamos,
ahora sí, to trabajar.

Between tanto, ella is interna
between the cortinajes and ¡oh aguja of my days
desgarrados! is sienta to the orilla
of a costura, to coserme the costado
to his costado,
to pegar the botón of esa camisa,
that is ha vuelto to caer. But hase visto!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Espergesia
translations.text:
I nací a day
        that Dios estuvo enfermo.


        All saben that vivo,
        that soy bad; and not saben
        of the diciembre of ese enero.
        For I nací a day
        that Dios estuvo enfermo.


        There is a vacío
        in my aire metafísico
        that nadie ha of palpar:
        the claustro of a silence
        that habló to flor of fire.


        I nací a day
        that Díos estuvo enfermo.


        Hermano, escucha, escucha…
        Good. And that not me vaya
        without llevar diciembres,
        without dejar eneros.


        For I nací a day
        that Díos estuvo enfermo.


        All saben that vivo,
        that mastico… And not saben
        for what in my verso chirrían,
        oscuro sinsabor of féretro,
        luyidos vientos
        desenroscados of the Esfinge
        preguntona of the Desierto.
        All saben… And not saben
        that the light is tísica,
        and the Shadow gorda…
        And not saben that the Misterio sintetiza…
        that él is the joroba
        musical and sad that to distancia denuncia
        the paso meridiano of the lindes to the Lindes.


        I nací a day
        that Dios estuvo enfermo,
        grave.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Here, Ramón Collar
translations.text:
Here,
Ramón Collar,
prosigue your familia soga to soga,
is sucede,
in tanto that visitas, tú, allá, to the siete espadas, in Madrid,
in the frente of Madrid.

¡Ramón Collar, yuntero
and soldado until yerno of your suegro,
marido, hijo limítrofe of the old Hijo of the Man!
Ramón of pena, tú, Collar valiente,
paladín of Madrid and for cojones; Ramonete,
here,
the tuyos piensan mucho in your peinado!

¡Ansiosos, ágiles of weep, when the lágrima!
¡And when the tambores, andan; hablan
delante of your buey, when the earth!

¡Ramón! ¡Collar! ¡To ti! ¡Si eres herido,
not seas bad in sucumbir: ¡refrénate!
Here,
your cruel capacidad is in cajitas;
here,
your pantalón oscuro, andando the time,
knows already andar solísimo, acabarse;
here,
Ramón, your suegro, the old,
you pierde to cada encuentro with his hija!

¡You diré that han comido here your carne,
without saberlo,
your pecho, without saberlo,
your pie;
but cavilan all in your pasos coronados of polvo!

¡Han rezado to Dios,
here;
is han sentado in your cama, hablando to voces
between your soledad and your cositas;
not sé who ha tomado your arado, not sé who
was to ti, ni who volvió of your caballo!

¡Here, Ramón Collar, in fin, your amigo!
¡Salud!, man of Dios, mata and escribe.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXI - Esta night desciendo of the caballo
translations.text:
Esta night desciendo of the caballo,
ante the door of the casa, where
me despedí with the sing of the gallo.
Is cerrada and nadie responde.

The poyo in that mamá alumbró
to the hermano mayor, for that ensille
lomos that había I montado in pelo,
for rúas and for cercas, child aldeano;
the poyo in that dejé that is amarille to the sun
my adolorida infancia... ¿And este duelo
that enmarca the portada?

Dios in the paz foránea,
estornuda, cual llamando también, the bruto;
husmea, golpeando the empedrado. Luego duda,
relincha,
orejea to viva oreja.

Ha of velar papá rezando, and quizás
pensará is me hizo tarde.
The hermanas, canturreando his ilusiones
sencillas, bullosas,
in the labor for the fiesta that is acerca,
and already not falta casi nothing.
Espero, espero, the heart
a huevo in his momento, that is obstruye.

Numerosa familia that dejamos
not ha mucho, today nadie in vela, and ni a cera
puso in the ara for that volviéramos.

Llamo of new, and nothing.
Callamos and us ponemos to sollozar, and the animal
relincha, relincha more todavía.

All están durmiendo for always,
and tan of lo more bien, that for fin
my caballo acaba fatigado for cabecear
to his vez, and between sueños, to cada venia, says
that is bien, that all is very bien.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Invierno in the batalla of Teruel
translations.text:
¡Cae water of revólveres lavados!
Precisamente,
is the gracia metálica of the water,
in the tarde nocturna in Aragón,
not obstante the construídas yerbas,
the legumbres ardientes, the plantas industriales.

Precisamente,
is the rama serena of the química,
the rama of explosivos in a pelo,
the rama of automóviles in frecuencia and adioses.

Así responde the man, así, to the death,
así look of frente and escucha of costado,
así the water, to the contrario of the blood, is of water,
así the fire, to the revés of the ceniza, alisa his rumiantes ateridos.

¿Who va, under the nieve? ¿Están matando? Not.
Precisamente,
va the life coleando, with his segunda soga.

¡And horrísima is the guerra, solivianta,
lo pone to uno largo, ojoso;
gives tumba the guerra, gives caer,
gives give a salto extraño of antropoide!
Tú lo hueles, compañero, perfectamente,
to the pisar,
for distracción your brazo between cadáveres;
tú lo ves, for tocaste your testículos poniéndote rojísimo;
tú lo oyes in your boca of soldado natural.

Vamos, for, compañero;
us espera your shadow apercibida,
us espera your shadow acuartelada,
mediodía capitán, night soldado raso...
For eso, to the referirme to esta agonía,
aléjome of mí gritando fuerte:
¡Abajo my cadáver!... And sollozo.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XLIX - Murmurado in inquietud, cruzo
translations.text:
Murmurado in inquietud, cruzo,
the traje largo of sentir, the lunes
                        of the verdad.
Nadie me busca ni me reconoce,
and until I he olvidado
                        of who seré.

Cierta guardarropía, sólo ella, us sabrá
to all in the blancas hojas
of the partidas.
Esa guardarropía, ella sola,
to the return of cada facción,
                        of cada candelabro
                        ciego of nacimiento.

Tampoco I descubro to nadie, under
este mantillo that iridice the lunes
                        of the razón;
and not hago more that sonreir to cada púa
of the verjas, in the loca búsqueda
                        of the conocido.

Buena guardarropía, ábreme
                        your blancas hojas:
quiero reconocer siquiera to the 1,
quiero the punto of apoyo, quiero
                        know of be siquiera.

In the bastidores where us vestimos,
not there is, not There is nadie: hojas tan sólo
                        of par in par.
And always the trajes descolgándose
for sí propios, of perchas
as ductores índices grotescos,
and partiendo without cuerpos, vacantes,
                        until the matiz prudente
of a gran caldo of alas with causas
and lindes fritas.
And until the hueso!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXV - Mother, me voy tomorrow to Santiago
translations.text:
Mother, me voy tomorrow to Santiago,
to mojarme in your bendición and in your crying.
Acomodando estoy my desengaños and the rosado
of llaga of my falsos trajines.

Me esperará your arco of asombro,
the tonsuradas columnas of your ansias
that is acaban the life. Me esperará the patio,
the corredor of abajo with his tondos and repulgos
of fiesta. Me esperará my sillón ayo,
aquel buen quijarudo trasto of dinástico
cuero, that for not more rezongando to the nalgas
tataranietas, of correa to correhuela.

Estoy cribando my cariños more puros.
Estoy ejeando ¿not oyes jadear the sonda?
                                      ¿not oyes tascar dianas?
estoy plasmando your fórmula of love
for all the huecos of este suelo.
Oh si is dispusieran the tácitos volantes
for todas the cintas more distantes,
for todas the citas more distintas.

Así, dead inmortal. Así.
Under the dobles arcos of your blood, for where
there is that pass tan of puntillas, that until my father
for ir for there,
humildóse until menos of the mitad of the man,
until be the primer small that tuviste.

Así, dead inmortal.
Between the columnata of your huesos
that not puede caer ni to lloros,
and to cuyo lado ni the destino pudo entrometer
ni a solo dedo suyo.

Así, dead inmortal.
Así.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Epístola to the transeúntes
translations.text:
Reanudo my day of conejo
        my night of elefante in descanso.


        And, between my, digo:
        ésta is my inmensidad in bruto, to cántaros
        éste is my grato peso,
        that me buscará abajo for pájaro
        éste is my brazo
        that for his cuenta rehusó be ala,
        éstas son my sagradas escrituras,
        éstos my alarmados campeñones.


        Lúgubre isla me alumbrará continental,
        mientras the capitolio is apoye in my íntimo derrumbe
        and the asamblea in lanzas clausure my desfile.


        But when I muera
        of life and not of time,
        when lleguen to dos my dos maletas,
        éste ha of be my estómago in that cupo my lámpara in pedazos,
        ésta aquella head that expió the tormentos of the círculo in my pasos,
        éstos esos gusanos that the heart contó for unidades,
        éste ha of be my body solidario
        for the that vela the soul individual; éste ha of be
        my ombligo in that maté my piojos natos,
        ésta my cosa cosa, my cosa tremebunda.


        In tanto, convulsiva, ásperamente
        convalece my freno,
        sufriendo as sufro of the lenguaje directo of the león;
        and, puesto that he existido between dos potestades of ladrillo,
        convalezco I mismo, sonriendo of my labios.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXVI - The verano echa nudo to tres años
translations.text:
The verano echa nudo to tres años
that, encintados of cárdenas cintas, to all
                                    sollozo,
aurigan orinientos índices
of moribundas alejandrías,
of cuzcos moribundos.

Nudo alvino deshecho, a pierna for there,
more allá todavía the other,
                                    desgajadas, and
                                    péndulas.
Deshecho nudo of lácteas glándulas
of the sinamayera,
good for alpacas brillantes,
for abrigo of pluma inservible
¡more piernas the brazos that brazos!

Así envérase the fin, as all,
as polluelo adormido saltón
of the hendida cáscara,
to light eternamente polla.
And así, from the óvalo, with cuatros to the hombro,
                                    already for what tristura.

The uñas aquellas dolían
retesando the propios dedos hospicios.
Of entonces crecen ellas for adentro,
                                    die for afuera,
                                    and to the medio ni van ni vienen,
                                    ni van ni vienen.

The uñas. Apeona ardiente avestruz coja,
from perdidos sures,
flecha until the estrecho ciego
                                    of senos aunados.

To the calor of a punta
of pobre sesgo ESFORZADO,
the griega sota of oros tórnase
morena sota of islas,
cobriza sota of lagos
in frente to moribunda alejandría,
to cuzco moribundo.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Light repentina
translations.text:
I estuve here antes,

not sé say how and cuándo:

conozco the prado detrás of the door,

the dulce aroma penetrante,

the sonidos susurrantes,

the luces to lo largo of the costa.

Tú has sido mía antes;

not sé say makes cuánto:

but apenas esa golondrina remontó,

and giró your cuello, algún velo cayó;

and lo supe to the instante.


¿Había sido así antes?

¿Not será that the vuelo concéntrico

of the time restaure nuestras vidas,

nuestro love, to pesar of the death,

and us traiga other deleite night and day?


Ahora, entonces, ¡with fortuna other vez!

¡Duerman my eyes the agitación of your cabellos!

¿Not yaceremos as hemos yacido,

and así, for love of Love,

the dormir and the despertar

not rompan already his cadenas?




“Sudden light”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Still siendo child, of aquel pain that damos...
translations.text:
Still siendo child, of aquel pain that damos

To the muertos poco in his heart pudo encontrar,

Without necesidad of pensamiento, toward his mente clara

Ellos retornan to die, and él to his life:

Still when the alas of a new love,

To lo largo of his plumas of torbellino,

Sonríen to the recibir the viento of the aurora,

Without disfrutes futuros, echa a mirada atrás,

Where the night sacude aquel old love fugitivo.


There is a cambio in the memoria of cada hora,

Vemos the última prímula of the campos

When the primeras amapolas brotan to the romper the day.

¡Pain for the cambio of the horas!

¡Pain for all the amores

That of his hand cayeron

For the orgullo of his juventud,

As the cuentas of a rosario dicho!




“Pride of Youth”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: With cálida aflicción, to the fin is deshizo the largo beso...
translations.text:
With cálida aflicción, to the fin is deshizo the largo beso:

and as the últimas gotas repentinas caen

of the resplandeciente alero when the tormenta ha huido,

to solas vaciló the latir of his corazones.

His pechos is apartaron, with the brotar abierto

of the flores nupciales to his lado, extendidas

from the tallo unido, more still his bocas ardiendo

is acariciaron where yacían separadas.


The sopor the hundió more profundamente that the marea

of the sueños, and his sueños the vieron sumergirse

and escapar. Delicadas his almas flotaron of new

for esplendores acuáticos, and, ahogados, grises

objetos of the day; until that for a prodigio

of leños nuevos and corrientes él is despertó and more

is maravilló: for ella estaba to his lado.




“Nuptial Sleep”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Of the niñez to the juventud; of the juventud to the ardua hombría...
translations.text:
Of the niñez to the juventud; of the juventud to the ardua hombría;

Of the letargo to the fiebre of the heart;

Of the life fiel to soñar with sombríos and perdidos days;

Of the confianza to the duda; of the duda to the borde of the prohibición;

Estos cambios han pasado as a ráfaga cíclica

Until ahora. ¡Oh, The Soul! Cuan rápido debió

Aceptar his primitiva inmortalidad,

¿Is that the carne reencarna in the polvo of dónde comenzó?


¡Oh, Señor of the trabajo and the paz! ¡Señor of the life!

¡Oh, Señor, horrible Señor of the voluntad! Aunque sea tarde,

Renovad esta soul with the obediente aliento:

That when the paz is reúna with the furia,

The trabajo is recupere, and the voluntad resurja,

Esta soul tal vez vea your rostro: Oh, Señor of the Death.




  “The Heart of the Night”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Mediodía silencioso
translations.text:
Your hands descansan abiertas over the hierba fresca,

Your dedos brotan of the earth as flores rosadas:

Your eyes sonríen in paz. The pasto resplandece absorto

In the olas nebulosas of the sky, that is reúnen in calma.

All rodea nuestro nido, until where the ojo puede contemplar,

Dorados campos reales with bordes of plata,

There where the animales corroen the faldas of the espino.

Este visible silence, inmóvil over the reloj of arena.


Profundo in the sun ansiado crece the libélula,

Colgando as a hilo azul lanzado of the sky:

Of manera that esta hora alada gotea over nosotros.

Oh, cerremos the corazones over este regalo inmortal,

Atrapemos esta inarticulada hora in compañía,

Dónde the silence of dos is transforma in a canción of love.




“Silent Noon”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To the igual that the hands arduas, the nubes débiles huyen...
translations.text:
To the igual that the hands arduas, the nubes débiles huyen

Of the vientos that arrasan the invierno of the aéreas colinas,

As multiformes e interminables esferas

That inundan the night in a súbita marea;

Terrores of ígneas lenguas, of inarticulado mar.

Incluso entonces, in algún sombrío cristal of nuestro aliento,

Nuestros corazones evocan the imagen salvaje of the Death,

Sombras and abismos that bordean the eternidad.


Without embargo, junto to the inminente Shadow of the Death

Is alza a Poder, that is agita in the ave or fluye in the corriente,

Dulce to the deslizarse, encantador to the volar.

Dime, my love. ¿What ángel, cuyo Señor is the Love,

Agitando the hand in the door,

Or in the umbral where yacen the trémulas alas,

Posee the esencia flamígera that tienes tú?




“Through Death to Love”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The belleza of the body
translations.text:
Is cuenta of the primera woman of Adán, Lilith,

(the hechicera to quien amó antes of recibir the regalo of Eva)

that his lengua engañaba antes that the of the serpiente

and his pelo embrujado was the oro primigenio.


Inmóvil permanece; joven, mientras the mundo is makes old;

and, delicadamente contemplativa of sí misma,

makes that the hombres contemplen the red brillante that teje,

until that heart and body and life in ella quedan presos.


The rosa and the amapola son his flores, for ¿dónde

podremos encontrar, oh Lilith, aquél to quien not engañen

your fragancias, your sutil beso and your sueños tan dulces?


Ah, in the mismo instante in that ardieron the eyes of the joven in the tuyos,

your embrujo lo penetró, quebró his altivo cuello

and retorció his heart with uno solo of your cabellos of oro.




“Body’s Beauty”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Delgadas son the faldas that the night dejó atrás...
translations.text:
Delgadas son the faldas that the night dejó atrás,

antes of that the day quiebre the sky with his crepitar.

Delgados son the jirones of the sueño,

oscilando in the espíritu cansado of the viento;

but in medio of aquel reposo inquieto

that desgarra the trama of the olvido and the recuerdo,

my soul is estira toward the tuya,

cada vez more cerca.


Nuestras vidas never is unen;

nuestros pensamientos never is distancian,

aquello that aferra your heart to the mío,

parece disolverse in a brillo sombrío.

Esta night, the Love ejerce a control total,

and with deseo and with pesar,

my soul is arrastra toward the tuya,

cada vez more cerca.


¿Existe a hogar, dónde the pesada Earth

is derrita in the aire brillante,

and dónde the mal not is respire;

dónde the water barra the eco of the sed,

and the fire sea the reflejo of nuestra fe?

Si the voluntad yace atada to the objetivo,

tal vez there pueda his esperanza engendrar.

My soul, in esta hora desolada,

is agita toward the tuya,

cerca, always a poco more.




“Insomnia”
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Miguel Ángel Osorio
translations.text:
Between my
		heart the penumbra of a calle,

		a reliquia, a aguijón, the eco of a voice.

		Between my heart -between my herida-,

		a caricia, the murmullo of the love.

		Between my heart -the desdeñoso-,

		the luna, a retrato, uno or dos nombres,

		the desamor también in my cloaca.

		In my heart the raíz of the insomnio and of the ira.

		Between my heart, hecho of fiebre,

		my soledad and my hermanos.

		Between my heart the pesadilla and the infierno,

		there the leve dicha and the esperanza.

		Between my heart alucinado, insecto of the night,

		the ebriedad of the instante,

		the revelación and the pureza,

		the abatimiento in my more roja entraña,

		the estupor and the entusiasmo in my silencioso heart.

		Between esta oscura claridad, between este vértigo,

		all my pavor, all my pena,

		all the desprecio entero and the love,

		all the embriaguez and the locura.

		Never ninguna fe in my heart ansioso.

		Ay, my delirante heart,

		ay my heart without asidero.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: I not soy Pedro
translations.text:
I not soy
		Pedro,
Juan,
ni Segismundo.


I not soy pura blood,
ni mestizo,
ni natural of the valle or of
		the estepa.


My pensamiento is a small mundo.
A mundo of orfandad of pura
		cepa.


Vine of not sé dónde,
a day in that unas hands
is estrecharon to
		medias.


And tú -poesía, viento-
ni lo haces more atroz,
ni lo remedias.


I not soy Gran Collar,
ni estoy sad,
ni creo in the derrota.


Admiro the rostro inmenso of the océano,
but prefiero the brill0

		of a gota.


Me gusta the verdad of the that esperan,
and the love
hecho life.


And creo in the retorno of the tiempos,
in other dimensión

		desconocida.


Recuerdo vagamente algunos signos,
algún destello of mitología,

		alguna forma gris of echar the suerte.


And not le tengo miedo to lo that venga:
ni to the ojo solapado of the
		life,
ni to the párpado sincero of the death.


I not soy the bandera,
ni the perdón,
ni the cayado.
Ni soy the
		that descubre,
ni the that salva
or reclama be salvado.
I not soy
		Pedro,
Juan,
ni Segismundo.


I soy a soplo of aire.
A sonido that passes.
The sonido fugaz
		of a milagro profundo.

For soy more that the carne misteriosa
in that alguien -a vez-

		me trajo to the mundo.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Esto ocurrió in a país of campesinos...
translations.text:
Esto ocurrió in a país of campesinos

in the altos Balcanes,

a grupo of colegiales

murió a death mártir in a solo day.


All habían nacido

the mismo año

and the escuela of the days was idéntica:

juntos habían recibido

iguales celebraciones,

all fueron vacunados

against the mismas enfermedades

and all murieron the mismo day.


Esto ocurrió in a país of campesinos

in the altos Balcanes,

a grupo of colegiales

murió of a death mártir in a solo day.


Cincuenta and cinco minutos

antes of the momento of die,

still sentados in his bancos,

aquel grupo small

resolvía the mismos difíciles problemas:

cuánto tarda a viajero

in atravesar to pie…

and etcétera.

His pensamientos estaban llenos

of the mismos números,

and his bolsos llenos of cuadernos

with buenas and malas notas inútiles.

The mismos secretos

patrióticos and románticos,

a puñado of sueños

estaba apretado in his bolsillos.

All pensaban that for mucho time,

muchísimo,

ellos correrían under the sky azul

until resolver todas the tareas of the mundo.


Esto ocurrió in a país of campesinos

in the altos Balcanes,

a grupo of colegiales

murió of a death mártir in a solo day.

The filas enteras of muchachos

is tomaron of the hand

and from the última clase

caminaron tranquilos toward the pelotón

as si the death not fuese nothing.

The filas enteras of amigos

subieron to the mismo time

to his eterna morada.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a pino
translations.text:
Pino esbelto and tranquilo,

soledad of the tarde,

tan concreto in the free

desolación of the aire,

tan alto when all

is confunde and abate

and huye the sun to your copa

tibio and agonizante.


How me fortalece

the paz of your combate,

ascensión without fatiga,

raíz honda and constante.


Your majestad envuelve

the sky without celaje

and in your recio sosiego

the earth is complace.


My eyes educados

in your sediento mástil

ascienden and divisan

the soledad more ágil,

mientras sueña the silence

without astros and without aves

as the solo decoro

of your green ramaje.


Pino esbelto and tranquilo,

your soledad you guarde,

and consagre the mía

desunida and errante,

segada of his earth,

extraña of his aire,

when still is oro virgen

the cumbre of the tarde

and tú clamas e invocas

the time of my carne

and other vuelo without time

that is sueña and is makes.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The miedo americano
translations.text:
The night imaginada

is porosa and with bocas

of Colt and parpadeos

of eyes tácitos. Has

his casas recogidas in madera

of desierto with perro. And there is crujidos

of arboleda  and serpiente

in a acecho black.

¿Is verdad? ¿The cuchillo,

the bala, the puño sordo,

the grito of muchacha violada

that expira, the paseante hecho despojo

and ahorcado  with his   cinto,

the millones of hands, of pupilas,

of pasos redoblantes, of centellas

with blood, son of the  sueño?

Was day    luciente

and a tumor cerebral atado to a rifle

subió  ala torre and explotó dejando

media milla of muertos.

The motor that makes pausa and roba to the child

necesita the light. Voy caminando

for esa esponja of the terror unido

to the “¡What more gives!” that traigo

from lejos, incrédulo.

Not veo more that brazos

of árbol amigo and light in lejanía,

and solo escucho the respiraciones

sosegadas llegando for a aire

of perfume and caricia

that sostiene the pálidas estrellas.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Existen estadísticas. Sabemos...
translations.text:
Existen estadísticas. Sabemos

cuántos corazones humanos is paran for minuto.

And vivimos in paz. También to the nuestro

le llegara his hora.

But estamos metidos in the salón of  espejos

where the mundo is makes.

In cada espejo afirma and us afirma

and lo afirmamos. When alguno quiebra

or is desluce repentinamente,

there is a largo vacío of tiniebla

as when the light is apaga in a discurso

and lo disuelve.

Ha llegado the hora and not ha llegado.

The espejo abolido abre other galería

that gives toward lo irreal and the mundo queda

as suspenso. Pronto reanuda

his imperio. Están the otros and until alguno

new for volvernos to the oficio

that not consuela lo that pierde.

Because quedamos empañados, vueltos,

in a vapor of niebla,

toward the galería tan profunda as the pain,

tan rica of fantasmas as the life misma

already casi for entero desovillada in nuestros pasos.

Caminando for ella,

recreando his escenarios with relieve sordo,

is va embotando lo that was punzante

as the sobrecarga of the latido

that is abulta in the soledad of the sufrimiento

and is makes already desgana of return to the presente.

Is endulza to more pain,

to pain apiadado,

volviendo the head with the eyes llovidos,

llevándonos to hablar with nuestros muertos.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Divagación
translations.text:
Si I not hubiera sido….

¿what sería in my lugar?


¿More lirios or more rosas?

0 chorros of water

or gris of serranía

or pedazos of niebla

or mudas rocas…


Of alguna of esas cosas, the more fría

me comes to the heart that the añora.

Si I not hubiera sido,

the soul mía repartida

pondría in cada cosa a chispa of love…


Nubes habría

more that otras nubes lentas…

(¡the nube that podría haber sido!…)

¿In the sitio, in the hora of what árbol estoy,

of what armonía more asequible and útil?


Esta shadow tan lejana parece that not is mía.

Me siento extraída in my ropaje

and rota in the aguas,

in the monotonía of the viento over the mar,

in the paz honda of the campo,

in the sopor of the mediodía!…


¡Who me volviera to the raíz remota

without light, without fin, without término and without vía!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Juegos of water
translations.text:
The juegos of water brillan to the light of the luna

as si fueran largos collares of diamantes:

The juegos of water ríen in the shadow… And is enlazan

and cruzan and cintilan dibujando radiantes

garabatos of estrellas…

There is that apretar the water There is that apretar the water

for that suba fina and alta… A temblor of espumas

the deshace in the aire; the return to unir… desciende

luego, abriéndose in lentos abanicos of plumas…


But not irá very lejos… Ésta is water sonámbula

that baila and that camina for the filo of a sueño,

transida of horizontes in fuga, of paisajes

that not existen… Soplada for a grifo small.


¡Water of siete velos desnudándote and never

desnuda! ¡Cuándo a chorro tendrás that rompa the broche

of mármol that you ciñe, and to the fin for a instante

alcance to traspasar as espada, the Night!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A love indeciso
translations.text:
A love indeciso is ha acercado to my door…

And not passes; and is queda frente to the door abierta.


I le digo to the love: – ¿What you trae to my casa?

And the love not responde, not saluda, not passes…


Is a love small that perdió his path:

Venía already the night… And with the night vino.


¡What love tan pequeñito for andar with the shadow!…

¿That word not says, what nombre not me nombra?…


¿What deja ir or separa? ¿That paisaje apretado

is le quedó in the fondo of the eyes cerrados?…


Este love nothing says… Este love nothing knows:

Is of the color of the viento, of the huella of a ave.


(…) Extraño love without rumbo that me gana and me pierde,

that huele the naranjas and that the rosas muerde…


That all lo confunde, lo deja… ¡And not lo deja!

That esconde estrellas nuevas in the ceniza vieja…


And not knows die ni live: And not knows

that the tomorrow is tan solo the today dead…

The cadáver futuro of este today claro, of esta hora cierta…

A love indeciso is ha dormido to my door…
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: In my oficio or my arte sombrío
translations.text:
In my oficio or my arte sombrío

ejercido in the night silenciosa

when solo the luna is enfurece

and the amantes yacen in the lecho

with todas his tristezas in the brazos,

junto to the light that sings I trabajo

not for ambición ni for the pan

ni for ostentación ni for the tráfico of encantos

in escenarios of marfil,

sino for ese mínimo salario

of his more escondidos corazones.


Not for the man altivo

that is aparta of the luna colérica

escribo I estas páginas of efímeras espumas,

ni for the muertos encumbrados

between his salmos and ruiseñores,

sino for the amantes, for his brazos

that rodean the penas of the siglos,

that not pagan with salarios ni elogios

and not hacen caso alguno of my oficio or my arte.

translations.title: Oh hazme a máscara
translations.text:
Oh hazme a máscara and a muro that me oculte of your espías

of esos agudos eyes esmaltados and of the garras ostentosas

of the rebeldía and the violación in the viveros of my rostro,

a mordaza of árbol, in silence golpeado for cubrirme of the desnudos enemigos

hazme a lengua of bayoneta in esta oración indefensa,

return my boca flagrante and that sea a trompeta of mentiras soplada dulcemente,

dame the facciones of a tonto moldeado in vieja armadura and roble

for escudar the cerebro brillante and confundir to the indagadores,

and a pain viudo manchado of lágrimas caído of the pestañas

for velar the belladona and make that adviertan the eyes secos

that otros traicionan the quejumbrosas mentiras of his pérdidas

with the pliegues of the boca desnuda and the risa solapada.

translations.title: Love in the manicomio
translations.text:
A extraña ha venido

to compartir my cuarto in esta casa that anda mal of the head,

a muchacha loca as the pájaros,


traba the door of the night with his brazos, his plumas.

Ceñida in the cama revuelta

alucina with nubes in esta casa to prueba of cielos,


until alucina with his pasos este cuarto of pesadilla.

free as the muertos

or cabalga the mares imaginarios of the pabellón of hombres.


Ha llegado posesa

the that admite the alucinante light to través of the muro saltarín,

posesa for the cielos


ella duerme in the canal estrecho, until camina the polvo,

until desvaría to gusto

over the mesas of the manicomio adelgazadas for my lágrimas.


And tomado for the light of his brazos, to the fin, my Dios, to the fin

puedo I of verdad

soportar the primera visión that incendia the estrellas.
